title: The Plaza Accord and Historical Causation
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
By the mid-1980s, the United States faced a strong dollar and large external imbalances, while trade friction with major partners intensified. In September 1985, finance officials from five industrial economies met in New York. Their statement supported further orderly appreciation of major currencies against the dollar, and the authorities used coordinated intervention to reinforce exchange-rate adjustment.

The dollar subsequently depreciated substantially against the yen and other currencies. Yet an exchange rate is not controlled by one meeting alone. Expectations, interest-rate differences, capital flows, trade positions, and later policy signals also influence currency markets. The agreement was an important coordination event, not a switch that mechanically fixed every later rate.

Yen appreciation put pressure on Japanese exporters and contributed to concern about slower demand. Japanese authorities eased monetary conditions, while firms, banks, borrowers, regulations, land-use expectations, and financial practices shaped the expansion of credit and asset prices. These links matter because saying “the agreement caused the bubble” compresses several decisions and feedback loops into a single arrow.

Good causal analysis asks a harder question: compared with what plausible alternative? Without the agreement, exchange rates and trade conflict might still have changed. With the agreement but different monetary, supervisory, or lending decisions, asset prices might also have followed another path. History cannot rerun the experiment, but it can identify mechanisms, timing, rival explanations, and evidence rather than treating sequence as proof.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: One international meeting mechanically determined every later exchange rate and asset price.

options.label: B
options.text: The agreement was irrelevant because markets never respond to policy coordination.

options.label: C
options.text: The agreement mattered, but later outcomes emerged through several policies, expectations, and feedback mechanisms.

options.label: D
options.text: A cause can be proved whenever it occurs before an outcome.

questions.answer: 正解：C。合意の重要性を認めつつ、後続政策・期待・フィードバックを含む多因子の連鎖を示します。Aは単一原因、Bは全否定、Dは前後即因果の誤りです。

questions.prompt: What exchange-rate adjustment did the agreement support?

options.label: A
options.text: Further orderly appreciation of major currencies against the dollar, reinforced by coordinated intervention

options.label: B
options.text: Permanent appreciation of the dollar against every currency

options.label: C
options.text: A legally fixed yen-dollar rate for all later years

options.label: D
options.text: The end of all official participation in currency markets

questions.answer: 正解：A。ドルに対する主要通貨のさらなる秩序ある上昇を支持し、協調介入で調整を補強しました。B～Dは方向・期間・政策手段を誤ります。

questions.prompt: A counterfactual is best defined as

options.label: A
options.text: an imagined alternative used for comparison

options.label: B
options.text: a confirmed accounting error

options.label: C
options.text: a secret exchange rate

options.label: D
options.text: a moral condemnation of borrowers

questions.answer: 正解：A。実際には起きなかったが因果比較の基準となる代替経路です。歴史では観測できないため、機構・時系列・証拠で妥当性を制約します。

questions.prompt: Which chain shows mechanisms omitted by the single arrow “agreement → bubble”?

options.label: A
options.text: Yen appreciation, export-demand concern, monetary easing, bank lending, regulation and land expectations, and credit-asset feedback

options.label: B
options.text: The meeting directly and automatically created every asset purchase

options.label: C
options.text: The agreement changed no expectations, policy, or lending decision

options.label: D
options.text: Asset prices rose before any relevant decision and without finance

questions.answer: 正解：A。円高、需要懸念、金融緩和、貸出、監督・規制、土地期待、信用と資産価格の相互増幅という中間機構があります。B～Dは連鎖を消します。

questions.prompt: Why does post-agreement dollar depreciation not prove that the meeting alone controlled exchange rates?

options.label: A
options.text: Expectations, interest-rate differences, capital flows, trade positions, and later policy signals also affected currency markets.

options.label: B
options.text: Exchange rates respond only to one meeting and never to markets.

options.label: C
options.text: The dollar did not depreciate after the agreement.

options.label: D
options.text: Recognizing other influences makes the agreement necessarily irrelevant.

questions.answer: 正解：A。為替には金利差、期待、資本移動、貿易、後続政策も作用します。合意の寄与を認めることと他変数をゼロとみなすことは別です。

questions.prompt: Why is temporal priority alone insufficient evidence of causation?

options.label: A
options.text: It does not rule out common causes, mediators, simultaneous policies, or show that the outcome would differ without the proposed cause.

options.label: B
options.text: A cause must always occur after its effect.

options.label: C
options.text: Any earlier event is automatically sufficient for every later outcome.

options.label: D
options.text: Mechanisms and rival explanations are irrelevant once dates are known.

questions.answer: 正解：A。前後関係だけでは共通原因・中間要因・同時政策を排除せず、反実仮想の差も示しません。B～Dは時系列を因果の十分条件と誤認します。

questions.prompt: Does noting that different monetary or supervisory policies were possible deny the agreement's importance?

options.label: A
options.text: No; it places the agreement within a causal chain and identifies later decision points that could have changed the outcome.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes; a cause must be the only possible cause to matter.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes; alternative later policies prove the agreement never occurred.

options.label: D
options.text: No; because later policies can never influence asset prices.

questions.answer: 正解：A。合意を連鎖の一部として位置づけ、別の選択で結果が変わり得た段階を示します。重要な寄与原因と唯一の原因は同義ではありません。

questions.prompt: What is the effect of describing the agreement as “not a switch”?

options.label: A
options.text: It rejects a model in which one policy action automatically fixes all later exchange rates.

options.label: B
options.text: It claims the meeting had no coordinating role.

options.label: C
options.text: It means officials literally used an electrical device to set the yen.

options.label: D
options.text: It proves every later rate was legally predetermined.

questions.answer: 正解：A。スイッチ比喩は、一度の操作で後の結果が自動決定する誤った因果モデルを可視化して退けます。B～Dは比喩と本文の立場を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which procedure best evaluates causation in a historical policy case?

options.label: A
options.text: Define cause and outcome, build a dated sequence, test mechanisms and rivals with records and data, compare plausible counterfactuals, and state uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.text: Find that the policy came first and declare it necessary and sufficient.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore contemporary records, economic data, and alternative explanations.

options.label: D
options.text: Treat contributing, necessary, and sufficient causes as identical.

questions.answer: 正解：A。定義、時系列、機構、競合原因、記録・データ、反実仮想、不確実性を順に検討します。B～Dは前後関係だけで因果の強さを過大評価します。
